## Description



The µTest++ framework provides overloaded comparison and logical operators to enable expressive and type-safe test assertions. These operators—such as <code>==</code>, <code>!=</code>, <code>&lt;</code>, <code>&gt;</code>, <code>&lt;=</code>, and <code>&gt;=</code>—are defined within the dedicated <code>micro&#95;test&#95;plus::operators</code> namespace to avoid conflicts with application-defined operators.



For standard values, the default operators are used, ensuring correct comparisons. However, when using the specialised µTest++ operators with typed operands, failed checks will display both the actual and expected values, greatly improving the clarity of test reports.



These operators are restricted to operands derived from the local <code>detail::op</code> type. For constant values, this is achieved using provided literals (e.g., <code>1&#95;i</code>), while dynamic values can be wrapped using casts such as <code>mt::to&#95;i&#123;expression&#125;</code>.



Logical operators (<code>&amp;&amp;</code>, <code>||</code>, <code>!</code>) are also supported and provide enhanced functionality when used with typed operands, allowing for the composition of complex test conditions in a natural and readable manner.




<SectionUser title="Examples">

</SectionUser>


<ProgramListing extension="cpp">

<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::test&#95;case (</Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;Operators&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">, [] &#123;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  </Highlight><Highlight kind="keyword">using namespace </Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">micro&#95;test&#95;plus::operators;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  </Highlight><Highlight kind="keyword">using namespace </Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">micro&#95;test&#95;plus::literals;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  mt::expect (compute&#95;answer () == 42&#95;i) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is 42 (with literal)&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  mt::expect (mt::to&#95;i &#123;compute&#95;answer ()&#125; == 42) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is 42 (with</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="stringliteral">cast)&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">; mt::expect (compute&#95;answer () != 43&#95;i) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is not 43&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  mt::expect (compute&#95;answer () &lt; 43&#95;i) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is &lt; 43&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  mt::expect (compute&#95;answer () &lt;= 43&#95;i) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is &lt;= 42&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  mt::expect (compute&#95;answer () &gt; 41&#95;i) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is &gt; 43&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">  mt::expect (compute&#95;answer () &gt;= 42&#95;i) &lt;&lt; </Highlight><Highlight kind="stringliteral">&quot;answer is &gt;= 42&quot;</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal">;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">&#125;);</Highlight></CodeLine>

</ProgramListing>




### Logical operators



Logical operators may be used in the same way as standard operators, with enhanced reporting available when used with typed operands.




<SectionUser title="Example">

</SectionUser>


<ProgramListing extension="cpp">

<CodeLine><Highlight kind="normal">mt::expect (compute&#95;answer () == 42&#95;i &amp;&amp; compute&#95;float () == 42.0&#95;f);</Highlight></CodeLine>

</ProgramListing>

This operator is intended for use with the framework&#39;s strongly-typed constants, wrappers, or other custom types, ensuring type-safe and expressive test assertions.

This overload of the greater than or equal operator enables comparison between two operands, where at least one is a local type derived from the local <code>op</code> base. It constructs a comparator object that can be used within the µTest++ framework to assert that the left hand side operand is greater than or equal to the right hand side operand. This operator is intended for use with the framework&#39;s strongly-typed constants, wrappers, or other custom types, ensuring type-safe and expressive test assertions.
